{{Short description|Temporary detention center for immigrant minors}}
{{Use American English|date=September 2025}}
The '''Tornillo tent city''' was a temporary immigrant detention facility for children located in [[Tornillo, Texas]] and operated by [[BCFS Health and Human Services|BCFS]] on behalf of the [[United States Department of Health and Human Services|Department of Health and Human Services']] [[Office of Refugee Resettlement]]. The department termed it an "emergency influx care facility" and named it the '''Tornillo Influx Facility'''.<ref>{{Citation|publisher=Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General|last=Levinson|first=Daniel R|title=The Tornillo Influx Care Facility: Concerns About Staff Background Checks and Number of Clinicians on Staff (A-12-19-20000)|date=2018-11-27|url=https://oig.hhs.gov/oas/reports/region12/121920000.pdf}}</ref> When it was built in June 2018, the capacity was 400 minor immigrants with a one-month contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tornillo-texas-tent-city-for-unaccompanied-migrant-children-to-remain-open-longer-than-planned/|title="Tent City" for unaccompanied migrant children to remain open longer than planned|website=www.cbsnews.com|date=9 July 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-24}}</ref> It was later expanded to a capacity of 4,000 minors. As many as 2,800 teenagers were held at the site before its closure was announced in January 2019. This made it one of the largest facilities in ORR's [[Unaccompanied Alien Children]] Program. All immigrant children had left the facility by January 11, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/politics/2019/01/11/tornillo-shelter-no-migrant-children-closed-january/2547461002/|title=Official: No migrant children remain at Tornillo tent shelter as it heads toward closure|date=January 11, 2019|website=El Paso Times|language=en|access-date=2019-07-01}}</ref> Nearly 6,200 minors cycled through the facility within the seven months it operated.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/immigration/trump-administration-to-shutter-texas-tent-city-for-migrant-teens/2019/01/11/c914356e-1510-11e9-b6ad-9cfd62dbb0a8_story.html|title=Trump administration removes all migrant teens from giant Tornillo tent camp|last=Sacchetti|first=Maria|date=January 11, 2019|newspaper=Washington Post}}</ref> The area was previously used for a few months in 2016 to process migrant families and unaccompanied minors.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/national-security/us-to-house-migrant-children-in-tents-outside-el-paso-as-government-takes-more-into-custody/2018/06/14/3dcff87e-7008-11e8-9ab5-d31a80fd1a05_story.html|title=U.S. to house migrant children in tents outside El Paso as government takes more into custody|last=MIroff|first=Nick|date=June 14, 2018|newspaper=Washington Post}}</ref>

== About ==
[[File:Tornillo_port_shelter_6_1529351187236.PNG_11953644_ver1.0_640_360.jpg|thumb|Bunk beds inside the tents]]
The tent city in [[Tornillo, Texas]] was created in order to "house the overflow of immigrant children, many of whom have been separated from their parents," according to [[NBC News]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/immigration/trump-admin-will-house-migrant-kids-tents-tornillo-texas-n883281|title=Feds to build tent city to house migrant kids in Tornillo, Texas|last1=Soboroff|first1=Jacob|date=14 June 2018|work=NBC News|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618000612/https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/immigration/trump-admin-will-house-migrant-kids-tents-tornillo-texas-n883281|archive-date=18 June 2018|last2=Kube|first2=Courtney|language=en-US|last3=Ainsley|first3=Julia}}</ref> It was run by the [[Administration for Children and Families]] which is a division of the [[United States Department of Health and Human Services]].<ref name="Herskovitz 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-immigration-tornillo/tent-city-for-migrant-children-puts-texas-border-town-in-limelight-idUSKBN1JG32L|title=Tent city for migrant children puts Texas border town in limelight|last=Herskovitz|first=Jon|date=20 June 2018|work=Reuters|access-date=2018-06-21|language=en-US}}</ref> The tent city was meant to be a temporary shelter and was the first one constructed to house children who have been separated from their families under Trump's "zero tolerance policy" for families entering the United States illegally.<ref name="Mekelburg 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/immigration/2018/06/14/trump-administration-picks-tornillo-tent-site-immigrant-kids/703455002/|title=Trump administration picks Tornillo as tent city site for immigrant children|last=Mekelburg|first=Madlin|date=14 June 2018|work=El Paso Times|access-date=2018-06-21|language=en}}</ref> United States Representative, [[Will Hurd]], said that "he was told that only teenage boys were at the facility -- and that they were children who had entered the country by themselves."<ref name="Aguilar 2018">{{Cite news|url=http://nmpolitics.net/index/2018/06/mayors-from-across-the-country-visit-tent-city-in-tornillo/|title=Mayors from across the country visit 'tent city' in Tornillo|last=Aguilar|first=Julian|date=21 June 2018|work=NMPolitics.net|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621213654/http://nmpolitics.net/index/2018/06/mayors-from-across-the-country-visit-tent-city-in-tornillo/|archive-date=21 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> However, U.S. Representative [[Beto O'Rourke]] said that children who were separated from their families were also housed in the tent city.<ref name="Aguilar 2018" /> It is unclear whether the minors housed in the tent city were separated from their families or had been apprehended without adults present.<ref name="Herskovitz 2018" />

The shelter was located near the [[Tornillo Port of Entry|Tornillo Land Port of Entry]] on the border of Texas and Mexico.<ref name="Parker 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.texastribune.org/2018/06/14/tent-city-tornillo/|title=Trump administration makes site selection for tent city near El Paso to house immigrant children separated from parents|last=Parker|first=Claire|date=2018-06-14|work=The Texas Tribune|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616190555/https://www.texastribune.org/2018/06/14/tent-city-tornillo/|archive-date=16 June 2018|language=en}}</ref> It was designed to start taking in 360 children, with further plans for expansion.<ref name="Parker 2018" /> The entire facility was built within 24 hours of the federal government confirming the location of the shelter.<ref name="Aguilar 2018" /> The location was confirmed on June 14, 2018, and by the next day, 100 children were already located on site.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.texastribune.org/2018/06/15/west-texas-facility-housing-unaccompanied-minors-and-running/|title=Trump administration opens tent city near El Paso to house separated immigrant children|last=Aguilar|first=Julian|date=2018-06-15|work=The Texas Tribune|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620134304/https://www.texastribune.org/2018/06/15/west-texas-facility-housing-unaccompanied-minors-and-running/|archive-date=20 June 2018|language=en}}</ref> The shelter had the capacity for 4,000 children.<ref name="Aguilar 2018" /> The shelter apparently doubled in size from June 18 to June 19, according to aerial photographs taken by [[Reuters]].<ref name="Herskovitz 2018" />

Tents housing the children were air-conditioned, according to a spokesperson from DHS.<ref name="Parker 2018" /> The tents could hold up to 20 children and 2 adults at a time.<ref name="Herskovitz 2018" /> The tents had bunk beds.<ref name="Herskovitz 2018" /> There was no shade in the area surrounding the tents.<ref name="Wright 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://weather.com/news/news/2018-06-20-tornillo-texas-tent-city-immigrant-children-temperatures-soar-above-100|title=Immigrant Children Arrive at Tornillo Tent City as Temperatures Soar Above 100|last=Wright|first=Pam|date=19 June 2018|work=The Weather Channel|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620235637/https://weather.com/news/news/2018-06-20-tornillo-texas-tent-city-immigrant-children-temperatures-soar-above-100|archive-date=20 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> The tent city facility also had showers, toilets, medical facilities, meeting spaces and fire trucks.<ref name="Wright 2018" /> It was fenced in with [[Chain-link fencing|chain link fencing]] topped with [[barbed wire]].<ref name="Jankowski 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.statesman.com/news/national-govt--politics/update-mayors-council-members-denied-entry-tornillo-tent-city/AmMcjpY2emI4EpJAVktbWP/|title=UPDATE: Mayors, council members denied entry to Tornillo 'tent city'|last=Jankowski|first=Philip|date=21 June 2018|work=Austin American-Statesman|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621231912/https://www.statesman.com/news/national-govt--politics/update-mayors-council-members-denied-entry-tornillo-tent-city/AmMcjpY2emI4EpJAVktbWP/|archive-date=21 June 2018}}</ref> There is one adult for every ten children and minors receive three meals a day and snacks.<ref name="Moore 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.texasmonthly.com/news/inside-texass-new-tent-city-children/|title=Inside Texas's New Tent City for Children|last=Moore|first=Robert|date=2018-06-16|work=Texas Monthly|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620134314/https://www.texasmonthly.com/news/inside-texass-new-tent-city-children/|archive-date=20 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> It has been estimated by DHS that it costs $775 per migrant child per night to house them inside the tent city.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2018/6/20/17482906/family-separation-border-tent-cities-cost|title=Report: "tent cities" for separated migrant children cost more than keeping them with their parents|last=Stewart|first=Emily|date=20 June 2018|work=Vox|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620211113/https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2018/6/20/17482906/family-separation-border-tent-cities-cost|archive-date=20 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/immigration-border-crisis/trump-admin-s-tent-cities-cost-more-keeping-migrant-kids-n884871|title=Tent cities cost millions more than keeping migrant kids with parents|last=Ainsley|first=Julia|date=20 June 2018|work=NBC News|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621172009/https://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/immigration-border-crisis/trump-admin-s-tent-cities-cost-more-keeping-migrant-kids-n884871|archive-date=21 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

On June 21, 2018, mayors from the [[United States Conference of Mayors|U.S. Conference of Mayors]] and politicians from across the United States were denied entry to the tent city.<ref name="Jankowski 2018" /> Hurd was able to tour the facility on June 15.<ref name="Moore 2018" />

== Operations ==
Operations were contracted to [[BCFS Health and Human Services]], a San Antonio faith-based nonprofit. Costs were estimated to be between $750-$1,200 for each minor per night.<ref name="Burke 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.kvia.com/news/border/number-of-migrant-children-living-at-tornillo-detention-center-grows/894700856|title=Number of migrant children living at Tornillo detention center grows|last=Burke|first=Garance and Martha Mendoza|date=2018-11-28|work=KVIA|access-date=2018-12-03|language=en-US}}</ref> As of November 2018, the 2,100 staffers had not passed FBI fingerprint background checks, a requirement waived by [[Scott Lloyd (lawyer)|Scott Lloyd]], now former director of HHS's Office of Refugee Resettlement.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/desert-detention-camp-for-migrant-kids-still-growing/2018/11/27/a6d01a34-f25d-11e8-99c2-cfca6fcf610c_story.html|title=US waived FBI checks on staff at growing teen migrant camp|newspaper=Washington Post|language=en|access-date=2018-12-03}}</ref>

BCFS has operated facilities for unaccompanied migrant minors in multiple states since the Obama administration.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://time.com/3066459/unaccompanied-minor-immigration-border/|title=This Baptist Charity Is Being Paid Hundreds of Millions to Shelter Child Migrants|last=Altman|first=Alex and Elizabeth Dias|date=August 4, 2014|magazine=Time|language=en|access-date=2018-12-03}}</ref>

== Criticism ==
Texas State Senator [[José R. Rodríguez]] called housing children in the shelters "totally inhumane and it is outrageous."<ref name="Mekelburg 2018" /> The area was currently experiencing 100 to 105 degrees [[Fahrenheit]] weather.<ref name="Mekelburg 2018" /> Texas State Representative [[Cesar Blanco|César Blanco]] said that housing immigrant children in tents was "dehumanizing and tarnishes Texas' tradition of welcoming immigrants."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2018/06/15/tent-cities-immigrant-children-texas-backlash/705562002/|title='Abhorrent': Texas officials, advocates decry placing immigrant children in tent cities|last=Jervis|first=Rick|date=15 June 2018|work=USA TODAY|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618214219/https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2018/06/15/tent-cities-immigrant-children-texas-backlash/705562002/|archive-date=18 June 2018|language=en}}</ref>

United States Representative [[Beto O'Rourke]] led hundreds on a protest march to the site of the tent city on June 17, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/national-international/Tornillo-Tent-City-Separated-Children-Protest-March-485784561.html|title=Marchers Protest at Site of 'Tent City' for Separated Children|last=Montes|first=Aaron|date=17 June 2018|work=NBC Bay Area|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621215553/https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/national-international/Tornillo-Tent-City-Separated-Children-Protest-March-485784561.html|archive-date=21 June 2018|language=en}}</ref>

US Representatives [[Rosa DeLauro]] (of Connecticut) and [[Lucille Roybal-Allard]] (California) called for the closure of the camp in a December 3, 2018 letter to HHS Secretary [[Alex Azar]]. In the letter, they stated, "The administration is using this facility, which is on federal land and unregulated by State child welfare authorities, to evade requirements and standards for the care of children."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/local/el-paso/2018/12/04/tornillo-closure-after-investigation-trump-administration-letter/2204099002/|title=Congresswomen call for immediate closure of Tornillo tent shelter for migrant children|date=December 4, 2018|website=El Paso Times|language=en|access-date=2018-12-07}}</ref><ref>Rosa De Lauro and Lucille Roybal-Allard, [https://delauro.house.gov/sites/delauro.house.gov/files/DeLauro-Roybal-Allard_Tornillo_Letter.pdf Letter to Alex Azar], December 3, 2018.</ref>

== Closure ==
According to [[Kevin Dinnin]], president of [[BCFS Health and Human Services|BCFS]], the camp closure initiated after the contractor refused to continue expanding operations. The day after the refusal, [[United States Department of Health and Human Services|Department of Health and Human Services]] announced that the strict background requirement for sponsor households would be reversed, expediting the rate of sponsorship placements.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/head-of-controversial-tent-city-says-the-trump-administration-pressured-him-to-detain-more-young-migrants/|title=Head of controversial tent city says the Trump administration pressured him to detain more young migrants|last=Green|first=Emily|date=2019-01-17|website=Vice News|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref> It was announced that all detained children had been sponsored or transferred to other shelters on January 11, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/politics/2019/01/11/tornillo-shelter-no-migrant-children-closed-january/2547461002/|title=Official: No migrant children remain at Tornillo tent shelter as it heads toward closure|website=El Paso Times|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref>
